about: Household composition, pets, resident profiles and the smart-home tier for generation-2 houses (docs/design/TIER1_SWEEP.md sections 12, 14.3 and 14.7), read by house_sim/generator/profile.py. Every table carries a source or says 'assumption'. Shares were transcribed offline from the surveys named (rounded; verify before quoting); they are the realistic default, not a benchmark-balanced one (open question 4 of the sweep).

presets.doc: weight: share of random draws (0 = only by name, {"composition": name}). adults/children/elderly: [min, max] counts with count_weights (index = count - min). adult_age / elderly_age: [min, max] years. relation: how the adults relate (roommates get separate bedrooms and strict ownership). child_age: [min, max] years for the children (default 0-17, a child of age < 1 is an infant).
presets.source: US Census Bureau, Current Population Survey 2023, America's Families and Living Arrangements (tables H1 and HH-1): one-person households about 29 % (about 12 % of all households are a person 65+ living alone), married-couple households about 47 % (about 18 % with own children under 18), other family households about 17 % (single parents about 8 %), nonfamily households of two or more about 7 %; multigenerational households about 5 % (Census ACS). Cohabiting couples are folded into 'couple'; 'other family' households (adult siblings, a grown child living with a parent) into 'couple' and 'multigenerational'.

family_counts_source: Children per family with children under 18: one about 42 %, two about 38 %, three about 15 %, four or more about 5 % (CPS 2023 table FM-3, rounded); single-parent families are smaller (assumption 55/30/15).

roles.doc: Child ages are drawn uniformly over [min, max] (US children under 18 are spread nearly evenly over single years of age, Census population estimates); roles follow the people domain's values. An infant's age is drawn in months (2-11) so it is never 0.
roles.elderly_from_age_source: every resident aged 70 or more is the people domain's 'elderly' (slower gait, higher fall risk, lower reach, heat vulnerability, early chronotype), householders as well as grandparents; the presets' and generation 1's elderly already start at 70-72. Householders keep authority 2 and their resident_N ids and share the primary bedroom with a partner; a grandparent has authority 1 and an elder_N id

elderly_abilities.doc: abilities of an elderly resident drawn by age band ('from': the first age of the band; mobility devices, low vision and reduced hearing are independent draws). Generation 1 keeps its uniform draw (layout.default_residents)
elderly_abilities.source: mobility devices: National Health and Aging Trends Study 2011-12 (Gell et al., J Am Geriatr Soc 2015): about 24 % of community-dwelling people 65+ used one in the last month (cane about 17 %, walker about 12 %), rising from about 15 % at 70-74 to about half at 85+; low vision (cannot recognise a face across the room or read newsprint with glasses): about 5 % at 70-74 to about 20 % at 85+ (NHATS self-report; Eye Diseases Prevalence Research Group 2004 for the rise with age); reduced hearing (hearing loss of 25 dB or more): about 45 % in the early 70s to about 80 % at 85+ (Lin et al. 2011, NHANES). Rounded; verify before quoting. The generation-1 draw gave every elderly resident a 1 in 3 chance of a walker

pets.doc: Probability that a household keeps the species (independent draws), per region; count_weights for dogs and cats (index = count - 1). Caged species are recorded in household.profile.pets_pending for the pets domain's generation-2 furnisher (aquarium, cage, terrarium, coop) and are not materialized as pet records until it lands; chickens need a backyard.
pets.source: us: AVMA Pet Ownership and Demographics Sourcebook 2017-2018 (dogs about 38 %, cats about 25 %, birds about 3 %) with APPA National Pet Owners Survey 2023-2024 for the order of fish, small animals and reptiles; uk: PDSA Animal Wellbeing (PAW) Report 2023 (dogs about 29 %, cats about 24 %); eu: IVH/ZZF German pet market 2022 (cats about 26 %, dogs about 21 % of households); jp: Japan Pet Food Association national survey 2023 (dogs about 9 %, cats about 9 %); ca: Canadian Animal Health Institute 2022 (about 60 % of households have a dog or a cat). Backyard chickens: USDA APHIS 2013 urban chicken survey (under 1 % of households in four US cities; 2 % here as an assumption including suburban yards). Rows not named in a source are assumptions anchored on these orders of magnitude.

dog_size_weights.source: assumption (small breeds lead US registrations; large breeds are about a quarter)

names.doc: Given names per region (labels only; never ids). Pools are deliberately gender-neutral and common; assumption.

smart_home.source: assumption from TIER1_SWEEP 14.7 (to be cited or revised; Parks Associates and Statista put US smart-device adoption in this range); electrical's generation-2 furnisher places the devices of the tier

tidiness.doc: Beta(a, b) draw per role, 0..1 (1 = everything always back home); assumption: adults and the elderly tidier on average than teens and children

chronotype.doc: Morningness-eveningness: about a quarter early, half intermediate, a quarter late in adults; adolescents are the latest group (Roenneberg et al. 2004/2007, Munich ChronoType Questionnaire); older adults the earliest

sleep.doc: bed and wake times (HH:MM) per chronotype; minors follow age (people domain: under 6 in bed by 19:30, older children 20:30)

diet.doc: share of adults; children follow the first adult's diet with probability 0.9 (assumption). Gallup 2018 (US vegetarian about 5 %, vegan about 3 %); YouGov tracker UK about 7 % vegetarian; pescatarian share assumption

allergies.doc: prevalence of a convincing food allergy per allergen, adults and children (Gupta et al., JAMA Network Open 2019 for adults; Pediatrics 2018 for children); independent draws

hot_drink.doc: usual hot drink of an adult; assumption per region (coffee leads in the US, Canada and Germany, tea with milk in the UK, green tea in Japan)

fold_style.doc: the textiles domain's fold styles (household.fold_style keys); assumption: even shares

tech_level.doc: assumption: Pew Research smartphone and tablet adoption falls with age (smartphone about 97 % under 50, about 76 % at 65+)

weekly_pattern.doc: BLS Current Population Survey 2023: employment-population ratio about 80 % at 25-54 and 64 % at 55-64, labour-force participation about 19 % at 65+; about 16 % of wage earners work non-daytime shifts (BLS 2017-18); full-time remote about 12-15 % of workers (assumption from 2023-24 survey ranges). 'home' = not in paid work outside the home
